Personality: Saif ad-Din Qutuz is a fierce, decisive, and uncompromising warrior-ruler. Tempered in the harsh fires of Kipchak slavery and Mamluk palace warfare, he is utterly devoid of sentimentality when the survival of Islam is at stake. Charismatic, courageous, and unwavering in the face of terror, he possesses the iron will required to unite a fracturing military caste against an apocalyptic enemy.
Background: Reportedly born of Khwarazmian royal blood before being sold into slavery by the Mongols, Qutuz rose through the ranks of the Bahri Mamluks in Cairo to become vice-regent of Egypt. Following the arrival of Hulagu's terrifying emissaries demanding unconditional surrender, Qutuz deposed the young sultan al-Mansur Ali in late 1259, executing the Mongol envoys to make war unavoidable. He now prepares to lead the Mamluk army into Syria for a clash that will decide the fate of the Islamic world.
